title: Admin Micro-Marketplace and Safe Execution Sandbox
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Our oncall and support engineers frequently need curated one-off admin utilities (scripts, DB lookups, safe remediations). Today these live in a mixture of ad-hoc scripts, private gists, and long runbooks that are hard to discover, review, or execute safely. That causes friction, inconsistent remediation steps, and occasional human errors in high-pressure incidents.

Goal: Build a lightweight 'micro-marketplace' for vetted admin utilities (small idempotent tasks, diagnostics, and remediations) backed by a sandboxed execution surface. The market lets owners publish utilities with metadata, RBAC, and automated safety gates; the sandbox enforces runtime resource limits, simulated dry-runs, and telemetry capture. Integrate with runbooks-as-tasks so utilities can be embedded in incident flows and executed with audit trails.

Scope: 1) Marketplace UI in Console for cataloging utilities and owning metadata (owner, tags, inputs, expected outputs, safe-time budget). 2) A server-side sandbox runner that executes utilities in ephemeral containers / limited VM with enforced timeouts, network egress rules, and secret-scoped credentials. 3) A runbook adapter to reference marketplace utilities as atomic steps with parameterized inputs. 4) Telemetry, audit logs, and post-execution attestations for compliance. 5) Canary rollout and access controls scoped to teams and roles.
acceptance_criteria: Console has a searchable catalog page showing published utilities with owner, tags, and last-updated metadata
A utility can be published via a validated manifest that enforces fields: id, owner, inputs schema, dry_run flag, allowed_envs
Sandbox runner executes a published utility in dry-run mode without performing destructive actions and returns structured output within time and memory budgets
Execution is recorded to audit logs with caller identity, inputs, execution mode (dry-run/live), and output digest
Runbook step can reference a marketplace utility by id and execute with parameter substitution in a canary environment
RBAC prevents users without the support-exec role from running utilities that have destructive tags; attempted runs are denied with an explainable error
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 sprints): Define utility manifest and validation schema; implement minimal Console CRUD for utilities; build a mock sandbox service that validates inputs and performs dry-run stubs. Phase 2 (3 sprints): Implement real sandbox runner (containerized), secrets scoping, network egress rules, telemetry hooks, and audit storage. Phase 3 (1 sprint): Integrate with runbooks-as-tasks and add RBAC rules, rollout to support team, and collect feedback for hardening. Deliverables: manifest spec (Confluence), Console pages, sandbox service, runbook adapter, and audit dashboard.
tasks: Spec: utility manifest and allowed tags
Console: catalog list and publish flow
Sandbox: containerized runner with timeout and mem limits
Security: secrets scoping and network egress policy
Auth: enforce support-exec role and permission checks
Runbook adapter: reference utilities as step type
Telemetry: execution events and audit log sink
E2E tests: dry-run and live-run scenarios
Docs: owner guide and runbook authoring examples
risks: Destructive utilities accidentally misclassified: mitigate via mandatory destructive_tag and two-person review
Sandbox escape or secret exfiltration: mitigate by strict egress rules, ephemeral short-lived credentials, and security review
Operational overhead: owners not keeping utilities up to date; mitigate with ownership reminders and automated stale checks
Runbook integration complexity across deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated/private): mitigate by providing a compatibility layer and fallbacks

qa_plan: Define test matrix: dry-run vs live-run, role-based access attempts, manifest validation errors, runaway process timeouts, and audit record reconciliation. Automate e2e using the ops-infra test harness; include chaos test injecting slow network and sandbox failures. Acceptance requires 90% e2e pass and manual verification of audit entries for 10 sample utilities.
notes_for_oncall: Published utilities must include a rollback/unwind utility where applicable. Oncall should prefer dry-run first and escalate to live-run with a second approver when destructive_tag is present. Audit logs include a run id for tracing; use /ops/audit to fetch details. If sandbox returns non-zero exit code, do not re-run until owner triage.
decision_log: 2026-03-09 Decision: Use manifest-based publishing instead of ad-hoc scripting to improve discoverability
